summary: CWE-379 fix: the bad() method created a temporary file inside a hard-coded, predictable, world-accessible directory (C:\testcases\insecureDir or /home/user/testcases/insecureDir/), which an attacker can anticipate and pre-create or tamper with. The repair removes the hard-coded insecure directory and instead creates the temp file via File.createTempFile with the two-argument form, which places it in the JVM's secure default temporary directory (java.io.tmpdir) under a randomly generated, unpredictable name. The existing owner-only readable/writable and non-executable permission hardening, the write of data, and the cleanup logic are all preserved, so legitimate functionality is unchanged.
